Your beginning

Slake bench

You begin an adult life with no gift, a pit, three lumps of quicklime, three jars of water and six dough rounds.

Lime yard

Your opening: A lime yard with a pit and a plate. Slaking lime makes heat; the plate bakes on it. Nothing here is a gift, only the reaction.

Slake one measure of quicklime with water · heat

Quench one measure of quicklime in one measure of clean water. The reaction conserves mass: it leaves slaked lime and releases heat, which the bench banks as 2 units of reserve (the reserve holds six; extra heat is lost to the air). It also strains the pit.

Available.

Time quote: Immediate.

Inputs: 1 × Quicklime, 1 × Clean water.

Slake one measure of quicklime with water · heat
Bake dough on the heated plate · uses heat

Press a dough round on the plate. Baking spends two units of the pit’s heat reserve and strains the plate; with no heat banked the plate stays cold.

Unavailable.

Time quote: Immediate.

Inputs: 1 × Dough round.

Recover enough energy before using this method.

Bake dough on the heated plate · uses heat
Let the plate cool

Leave the plate to cool and settle. It clears the strain from baking; it adds no heat.

Available.

Time quote: 3 played minutes.

Inputs: None quoted.
